question.problem:
Calculate the value of 
$\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & -2 & 3 \\ -1 & -1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}|.$

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries below ${a}_{11}$ equal to zero. You should be able to reduce the given $4\times 4$ determinant to a $3\times 3$ determinant.*
question.worked_solution:
Using elementary row operations, let's make entries below ${a}_{11}=1$ equal to zero.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & -2 & 3 \\ -1 & -1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $1$st column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{1+1}|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{2+1}|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(4-(-2)) \\  & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$
